assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: bug (two distinct, cited gaps); driver_capability: ready.

## Disambiguating three similarly-named muse record shapes

The corpus contains THREE structurally distinct 'task'-adjacent record families, and only one of them is the user-visible todo/task list this scenario tests:

1. **`kind:"task"` under the `runtime.session` envelope (payload_type="runtime.session", payload.kind="task")** — this is what produces the 1334-record count. Directly confirmed both by parser.go's own doc comment (lines 59-74: 'The task/tool_batch.effect.* families... describe the SAME tool calls as a lower-level effect execution view') and by muse-format-spec.md §4's full enumeration of its `task_kind` values on `proposed`: `tool.bash`, `model.meta.response`, `reminder.agent.skill-reminder`, `reminder.agent.goal-reminder`, `reminder.agent.verify-reminder`, `session_name.allocate`, `workflow.agent.native` (subagent spawn). Every one of those is internal WORK-UNIT bookkeeping for a tool call or an internal reminder/subagent lifecycle — never a user-authored todo item. This parser deliberately does not wire it (package doc, parser.go:57-74): tool-call open/close is read off the simpler assistant_tool_calls_committed/tool_result_batch_committed pair instead. Not the task list.
2. **`runtime.session.task` (a separate, top-level payload_type, NOT nested under `runtime.session`)** — muse-format-spec.md §4 states directly: 'tracks session-scoped bookkeeping tasks (not tool calls per se) — the only kind seen: `session_name.allocate`'. Internal session-naming bookkeeping. Not the task list.
3. **`todo_snapshot_updated` (an `event.kind` value nested under `runtime.session`→`kind:"run"`)** — THIS is the user-visible todo/task list. Confirmed with a direct, fresh scan of the live corpus on this machine (not just the format-spec doc, which lists the event.kind name but never dumped its shape): `find ~/.local/share/muse/sessions -name session.jsonl -exec grep -l todo_snapshot_updated {} \;` finds it in exactly one live session tree (`01a09c47-506a-7763-b82a-9ab89a9e195a`), with 4 top-level occurrences (revisions 1-4) plus matching copies folded into subagent tool-output chunks. Each record carries `event.kind:"todo_snapshot_updated"`, `event.revision` (a monotonic counter), `event.source_tool:"write_todos"` (the literal tool name), and `event.items[]` — an array of `{text, status}` objects. The four captured revisions on this machine show a real 5-item list walking through every status: revision 1 has item 1 `in_progress`/items 2-5 `pending`; revision 2 has item 1 `completed`, item 2 `in_progress`; revision 4 has items 1-2 `completed`, item 3 `in_progress`. This is a full-snapshot-replace shape (the whole current list re-sent every call, no incremental delta, no stable per-item id — items are keyed by their literal `text`), structurally identical to OpenCode's `todowrite` (core/adapters/inbound/agents/opencode/parser.go:261-333, `appendTodowriteDeltas`) and NOT like Claude Code's TaskCreate/TaskUpdate (which has a stable per-item id from the start). Independently corroborated by prior wire-schema research (muse-capabilities.md, `task_list` section): 'Wire schema: TodoItem(text, status), TodoListState, session/todoListChanged — the fold of... a durable TodoSnapshotUpdated record landed... the full todo list, replaced wholesale. A first-class, durable structured-task-list mechanism.'

## agent_supports: yes

Muse has a first-class `write_todos` tool that rewrites the whole todo list on every call, durably logged via `todo_snapshot_updated`, exactly matching this scenario's shape (create 3 items, walk each pending→in_progress→completed). The live corpus sample shows this exact arc happening organically (a real onboarding-factory work session tracking its own multi-step task list).

## daemon_capability: bug — two distinct, independently-cited gaps

**Gap 1 — the todo signal itself is never wired.** `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`'s `parseRunEvent` (lines 267-304) dispatches on `event.kind` under `kind:"run"`; `todo_snapshot_updated` falls into the `default` arm (line 295 names it explicitly, among other 'high-volume internal bookkeeping this stage has no use for') and returns `ev.Skip = true`. So `SessionMetrics.Tasks` (`core/domain/session/metrics.go:363`, the exact API field this scenario's acceptance criteria need — 'Three task items appear in the session API tasks field') is NEVER populated for muse today, even though the durable trace exists (`durability:"durable"`, `record_type:"event"` on the live-captured records). This is a trace-exists-but-daemon-ignores-it gap, not an architectural incapability: the exact reusable mechanism already exists in the codebase for an IDENTICAL shape — `core/pkg/tailer/todo_reconciler.go`'s `TodoReconciler` (full-snapshot reconciliation keyed by content, no stable id), currently used only by the opencode adapter for its structurally-identical `todowrite` snapshots. Wiring muse's `todo_snapshot_updated.items[]` through the same reconciler (keyed by `text`, mapped to `Todo{Key: text, Status: status}`) is the fix shape; the format-spec's independent 'session/todoListChanged' wire-schema note names the same target shape muse's own MSP protocol describes.

**Gap 2 — muse's per-prompt reminder-agent children pollute SubagentCount for THIS scenario's own acceptance criterion.** This scenario's 3rd acceptance criterion is 'SubagentCount stays 0 (no child sessions spawned)' — the whole point of task-list is to prove a todo-list update is NOT a subagent spawn. But muse-format-spec.md §9 (independently corroborated by a LIVE recording, cited below) establishes that muse spawns internal `goal-reminder`/`verify-reminder` (and sometimes `skill-reminder`) micro-agent children for EVERY prompt via `memory_reminder_child_session_linked`, and these children get a real, materialized `<parent>/subagent/<child-id>/session.jsonl` on disk — the SAME nested directory shape a genuine `subagent.control.*`-spawned Agent-tool subagent gets. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/adapter.go`'s `parentSessionIDFromPath` (lines 161-191) derives parent-child linkage PURELY from that directory structure — it has no way to distinguish a reminder micro-agent's child directory from a genuine user-spawned subagent's, since it never reads `memory_reminder_child_session_linked`'s `reminder_agent_id` field (that event.kind is itself in the same Skip=true default arm as `todo_snapshot_updated`, parser.go:293). This was not just theorized: it was LIVE-CONFIRMED during this same onboarding pass, in the sibling cell `2-2_auto-executed-tool-call`'s own committed metadata.json (recording 2026-09-14-04-47-31, session `01a09dd0-0803-7961-bdd0-3fb88305d5ef`) — a reminder subagent's own read-only working→ready arc was captured as a REAL session in the daemon's session tree, distinct from the parent, with its own session id (`35c6c413-5c09-4c10-9b66-daee87a1d0d1`). Since every muse prompt (not just task-list prompts) triggers this, and irrlicht's `SubagentCount` (`platforms/web/formatters.js:312`, `activeSubagentCount` — literally `children.filter(state is working/waiting).length`) counts ANY linked child regardless of role, this scenario's `SubagentCount stays 0` criterion is expected to be VIOLATED by the current daemon for the full duration the reminder children are alive, for reasons entirely orthogonal to the todo-list feature itself.

Both gaps are daemon-side (a distinguishing trace exists in both cases — `todo_snapshot_updated`'s own event, and `memory_reminder_child_session_linked`'s `reminder_agent_id` field — the parser just doesn't read either), not agent limitations and not a 3-state-model incapability, so `bug` is the correct pillar value (not `incapable`). `record` should record known_failing and hand back an issue for both.

## driver_capability: ready

The recipe needs only `send` + `wait_turn` + `sleep`, all three genuinely implemented in `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`'s `DRIVE_ELICITS` (line 167: `send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean restart sigkill start_session session`). No new primitive required.

## Vacuous-pass condition

Under what condition would this cell pass while proving nothing? If `turn_start`/`turn_end` were left unpinned (no `same_session_as`), a reminder child's own working→ready arc could satisfy the phase match instead of the parent's — the EXACT mechanism that silently passed the sibling `2-2` cell against a subagent transcript before it was caught and fixed (see that cell's own committed caveats). This spec bakes the fix in from the start: every post-birth phase is pinned `same_session_as:session_birth`, which no reminder child can ever satisfy (format-spec §9: reminder children go straight to working, skipping the `ready` birth state entirely, so they can never BE `session_birth`).
caveats: KNOWN FAILING (documented target, not yet live-recorded): the session API's `tasks` field is expected to stay EMPTY for muse today (gap 1 above) instead of showing the three items with pending/in_progress/completed statuses the scenario's 1st and 2nd acceptance criteria require. The spec below still asserts the correct state-arc behavior; it does not weaken to match the bug.

KNOWN FAILING (documented target, not yet live-recorded): `SubagentCount` is expected to be nonzero for part of the recording (gap 2 above) — muse's own goal-reminder/verify-reminder children, not the write_todos calls, are the cause. This is a muse-wide per-prompt side effect, not specific to task-list, but task-list is the first muse scenario whose acceptance criteria actually assert SubagentCount==0, so it is the first cell this daemon gap is load-bearing for.

write_todos's own approval/policy path has never been directly observed in the corpus — no `kind:"task"` `task_kind` value resembling 'todo'/'write_todos' appears anywhere in the sampled sessions (muse-format-spec.md §4's enumeration), which is consistent with write_todos being a pure bookkeeping tool that bypasses the side-effect/approval tracking apparatus entirely (unlike `tool.bash`), matching claudecode/opencode's identical tools (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/todowrite are also un-gated). But this is an inference from absence, not a positive observation of a policy_decision on a write_todos call — UNVERIFIED, flagged for `record` to settle live.

Not yet recorded end-to-end for muse — 0 prior recordings of this cell. This verdict is grounded in the built adapter's code, the live corpus on this machine (fresh grep + full-record dump done for this assessment), muse-format-spec.md, muse-capabilities.md, and the sibling 2-2 cell's own live-recorded caveats — not a live run of THIS scenario's own recipe.

Session-birth timing (max_delay_ms:1000) is carried over from the sibling 2-2 cell's own live-recorded, empirically-validated bound (same single-birth launch mechanism, content-independent), not re-measured for this specific recipe.

sources.note: Found and dumped all 4 top-level todo_snapshot_updated records (revisions 1-4) in session 01a09c47-506a-7763-b82a-9ab89a9e195a: event.source_tool='write_todos', event.items[]={text,status}, statuses walking pending→in_progress→completed across revisions. This is the primary, direct evidence for the user-visible task-list shape.

Package doc confirms kind:"task" is the tool-call/effect-execution view (1334-record family); parseRunEvent's default arm (line 295) names todo_snapshot_updated explicitly among currently-unwired event kinds, Skip=true.
Parent-child linkage is derived purely from directory structure (<parent>/subagent/<child-id>/), with no role/reminder_agent_id filtering.

Evidence doc: distinguishes kind:"task" (tool-call bookkeeping) from runtime.session.task (session_name.allocate only) from todo_snapshot_updated (the actual todo list); documents that goal-reminder/verify-reminder children get real on-disk subagent/<id>/ directories for every prompt.
Independent wire-schema corroboration: TodoItem(text,status), TodoListState, session/todoListChanged, durable TodoSnapshotUpdated record replacing the full list wholesale. Confidence: high.

Sibling cell's own LIVE recording (2026-09-14-04-47-31, session 01a09dd0-0803-7961-bdd0-3fb88305d5ef) empirically confirms a reminder-agent child materializes as a real, independently-tracked session for an ordinary (non-task-list) prompt — the direct evidence for gap 2's SubagentCount pollution, and the source of the same_session_as pinning fix baked into this cell's spec.
The reusable full-snapshot-reconciliation mechanism (keyed by text, no stable id) already in the codebase for an identical shape — the fix target for gap 1.
SessionMetrics.Tasks []Task — the API surface this scenario's acceptance criteria assert on.
SubagentCount is literally children.filter(state==working||waiting).length — any linked child counts, regardless of role.
send/slash/wait_turn/sleep/exit_clean/restart/sigkill/start_session/session genuinely implemented; this recipe needs only send/wait_turn/sleep.
Sibling cells for the same scenario, templated for phase structure and recipe shape; opencode's is the closer structural analog (full-snapshot-replace tool, no stable per-item id).

preconditions: muse CLI on PATH and authenticated (muse login or META_API_KEY) — confirmed installed at 1.2.1 on this machine
irrlichd is recording (--attach or isolated coexist mode)
the default muse model/preset exposes the write_todos tool (observed live on this machine's default meta provider/preset — re-probe at record time if a different preset is pinned)
setup: Driver generates a fresh lowercased session UUID and a fresh cwd under <staging>/cwd/ (launch_repl, driver-interactive.sh)
Driver launches with --trust-workspace so the untrusted-workspace modal does not swallow the first message (defect #1 fix, commit 0239a1bd)

script.text: Use your todo list to track three short work items called item-one, item-two, and item-three. Walk each one from pending to in_progress to completed, one at a time, before moving to the next. Do this directly in this session -- do not spawn a subagent or delegate to another agent. When all three items are completed, reply with exactly the single word: done

verify: events.jsonl shows the session entering ready, then exactly one ready→working transition and one working→ready transition, both pinned to the SAME session that was born ready (same_session_as:session_birth) so a reminder-agent child's own arc cannot satisfy the match
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to waiting for this session during the entire run (write_todos is expected to be auto-executed, like TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/todowrite on the sibling adapters)
final session state is ready; transcript shows the literal final reply token 'done'

KNOWN FAILING, documented target: the session API's tasks field should list the three items with subjects matching item-one/item-two/item-three and status progressing pending→in_progress→completed — expected to be EMPTY today (daemon=bug gap 1, todo_snapshot_updated unwired)

KNOWN FAILING, documented target: SubagentCount should stay 0 for the whole run — expected to be nonzero while muse's own goal-reminder/verify-reminder children are alive (daemon=bug gap 2, reminder children indistinguishable from real subagents by the path-based linkage)
